html:
Stamford Raffles was a British colonial official of the East India Company who governed Java and founded modern Singapore as a free port in 1819.

During the Napoleonic Wars, Britain seized Java from the Dutch in 1811, and Raffles governed it until 1816. He tried to replace forced deliveries with a land tax, studied Javanese culture, and had the ruins of Borobudur cleared; see Borobudur built. He published The History of Java in 1817. Java was handed back to the Dutch.

As lieutenant governor of Bencoolen in Sumatra, he looked for a British port to rival the Dutch in the Strait of Malacca. In 1819 he made a treaty with a claimant to the throne of Johor and set up a trading post on Singapore island; see Founding of modern Singapore. It grew quickly as a free port without tariffs. The Anglo Dutch Treaty of 1824 confirmed it as British. Back in London he founded the Zoological Society. He died in 1826, on his 45th birthday. The giant flower rafflesia is named after him.
